categories.name: Knowledge & Understanding
criteria: Writing stays focused on the chosen side

categories.name: Thinking
criteria: Uses reasons with explanations (why/how) and relevant examples
Acknowledges at least one opposing viewpoint and explains why the chosen position is stronger

categories.name: Communication & Structure
criteria: One main argument per body paragraph
Each body paragraph includes explanation and an example
Conclusion reinforces the position and summarizes key points

counterpointMissingPenalty.note: If the essay does not include an opposing viewpoint/counterpoint, subtract points even if structure is otherwise complete.

scoreMeaning.description: Strong arguments with clear structure and mature development, as appropriate for the student's grade
Good position and structure; development or counterpoint needs improvement, as appropriate for the student's grade
Structure and/or argument development is incomplete; rewrite required, based on grade-level expectations
Major gaps in grade-level writing fundamentals and argument structure

gradingPrinciples: All evaluations must be based on expectations appropriate for the student's grade level.
Do not apply higher-grade or adult writing standards.
Apply spelling, vocabulary, and language conventions according to the specified language variant.
Because research is not required, do not penalize the student for not citing sources or including facts beyond common knowledge and personal experience.

softGuidelines: Prefer topics connected to student life or school life
Topics should be answerable without external research
